surfaces.current: The supported SDK path uses initialize and initialized on a 2025-era connection.
surfaces.next: The 2026-07-28 path uses server/discover and carries no initialize session state.
surfaces.rollback: Keep the published package on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0 and remove the opt-in probe lane.

surfaces.current: The bridge accepts an optional MCP session identifier in local configuration.
surfaces.next: Core requests are stateless and identity is supplied per request.
surfaces.rollback: Retain the current optional session field without sending it on the modern probe path.

surfaces.current: Caller identity and capability assumptions are connection-scoped by the stable SDK.
surfaces.next: Protocol version, client identity, capabilities, and trace context are carried in params._meta on each request.
surfaces.rollback: Disable modern negotiation and continue using the stable connection-scoped SDK behavior.

surfaces.current: The bridge does not depend on modern MCP method and name headers.
surfaces.next: HTTP requests bind MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, and tool-specific Mcp-Name to the body.
surfaces.rollback: Remove the modern HTTP adapter while preserving the existing A2A outbound policy.

surfaces.current: Agent cards are mapped deterministically to MCP tool definitions.
surfaces.next: tools/list remains available and adds cache hints plus modern response metadata.
surfaces.rollback: Keep the stable deterministic mapping and omit modern cache metadata.

surfaces.current: Tool calls pass the existing audience, tenant, scope, consent, policy, guardrail, and outbound checks.
surfaces.next: tools/call remains the invocation method and adds per-request metadata and header binding.
surfaces.rollback: Use the stable SDK call shape while retaining every existing security boundary.

surfaces.current: The bridge does not publish MCP cache lifetime or scope metadata.
surfaces.next: Cacheable results carry explicit ttlMs and cacheScope values.
surfaces.rollback: Return zero-lifetime private results or remain on the stable SDK path.

surfaces.current: Unsupported modern versions are outside the published support contract.
surfaces.next: Modern endpoints return a bounded error naming requested and supported versions.
surfaces.rollback: Reject modern negotiation before any tool execution and retain the stable SDK range.

surfaces.current: A2A request cancellation is covered by the runtime and transport contracts.
surfaces.next: MCP cancellation remains a notification and must not bypass A2A task authorization or audit policy.
surfaces.evidence: cancelled-notification.json and existing A2A cancellation tests
surfaces.rollback: Do not expose MCP cancellation until the bridge has an explicit authorized mapping.

surfaces.current: A2A trace propagation is handled by runtime telemetry boundaries.
surfaces.next: traceparent and tracestate may be carried in request metadata and must remain opaque and bounded.
surfaces.rollback: Ignore MCP trace metadata and preserve existing A2A propagation only.

surfaces.current: The bridge validates principal, audience, tenant, scopes, consent, tool policy, guardrails, and outbound destinations before network access.
surfaces.next: Transport authentication changes do not replace the bridge authorization boundary.
surfaces.rollback: Disable the modern transport while keeping the current fail-closed authorization implementation.

surfaces.current: MCP tasks are not part of the published bridge surface.
surfaces.next: Tasks are evaluated as a separate optional extension and are not inferred from A2A task support.
surfaces.evidence: Compatibility matrix decision only; no production route is registered.
surfaces.rollback: Remove the experimental task probe without changing A2A task behavior.

surfaces.current: MCP Apps are not part of the published bridge surface.
surfaces.next: MCP Apps remain a separate optional integration concern.
surfaces.evidence: Compatibility matrix decision only; no UI resource or app bridge is registered.
surfaces.rollback: Remove any future app experiment independently of the MCP tool bridge.

surfaces.current: The bridge does not invoke roots, sampling, or logging server-to-client request APIs.
surfaces.next: Deprecated server-request flows are not introduced; modern input-required flows require a separate design review.
surfaces.evidence: packages/mcp source inventory and the absence of these request registrations
surfaces.rollback: No rollback action is needed because the deprecated surfaces remain unused.
